story: During a time of famine, the chief sent out two scouts to hunt for food. As they traveled, they saw a white cloud in the distance, and from it emerged a beautiful young woman in white buckskin, with dark hair, dark skin, and dark eyes. One of the men was filled with lust for her and approached her, telling his companion he intended to claim her as a wife. The companion warned him she seemed to be a sacred woman and that disrespecting her would be dangerous, but he ignored this advice. The second man watched as the first embraced the woman, and a cloud enveloped them both. When it cleared, only the woman remained, along with a pile of the first man's bones. Frightened, the second man began to draw his bow, but the woman beckoned him forward, saying she could see into his heart and knew he did not share the first man's motives. Since she spoke his language, he believed she was of his people and approached. She revealed she was holy, possessing spiritual and supernatural power, and told him that if his people followed her instructions, they would rise again. He promised to obey. She instructed him to return to his camp, summon the Council, and prepare a feast for her arrival. She then taught the people seven sacred ceremonies meant to protect the Earth, and gave them a sacred ceremonial pipe. The ceremonies included a purification rite, a vision-seeking rite, a sun dance, a rite of making relatives, a female puberty rite, a ball-throwing rite, and a soul-keeping rite. Each part of the pipe—the stem, bowl, tobacco, breath, and smoke—symbolized the relationships between the natural world, the elements, humans, and the spiritual beings maintaining the cycle of the universe.
